document.title: 2016 X Trial Australian Championship
document.notes: Three image-only pages. Page 1 (Day 1, 8th April 2016) and page 2 (Day 2, 9th April 2016): four Qualifying Heat blocks and two FINAL Heat blocks, each with two riders ('Rider # n', 'Rider Name - ...'), six section marks, Race, Total, Place; and a 'Day n Results' table with Championship Points. 'Race Win = 0 / Race Second = 1' is printed above the heats. Page 3: 'Championship Results' with Day 1, Day 2 and Total points for the top four only, ties annotated '7 cleans' / '5 cleans'. The 'Rider #' changes from day to day and between qualifying and final, so it is a heat slot, not a riding number; day 2 qualifying slots follow the day 1 result (#1 = day 1 winner).

rule_sets.name: X Trial heats
rule_sets.notes: Heat Total = six section marks + Race. Ties: most cleans, printed as '4 cleans' / '3 cleans' and '7 cleans' / '5 cleans'; a race win counts as a clean. Whether Trial or Super Trial rules (MoMS 15.12.1.7) applied is not stated. Day and championship placings are by championship points (25, 22, 20, 18, then 0).

rule_sets.name: Head-to-head race in each heat
rule_sets.notes: The two riders of a heat race each other; the loser adds 1 to the heat total.

misfits.what: The day 2 Final was cancelled after one section of heat 1 ('Electrical storm forced the cancellation of the Final'). Sections have a 'cancelled' object but parts do not, so the cancellation sits in part.x_cancelled plus counts_toward_result=false; the per-rider heat status uses 'no-result' with the storm text as status_as_printed.
misfits.suggestion: Add part.cancelled {scope, reason, after} mirroring section.cancelled, and a status 'cancelled' for totals and rows.

misfits.what: The head-to-head Race point is a per-heat value, not a section. It is encoded as a 'race' section (kind race, own rule_set with values 0/1) so it sits in the grid beside the six marks; ride components or total.penalties would also work. The guide does not say which to use, so two mappers will encode it differently.
misfits.suggestion: Pick one encoding in the guide (part-level component such as total.components[{type: race}] is the most natural) and drop the others.

misfits.what: Printed clean counts include a race win (Race = 0) as a clean ('4 cleans' with three section zeros). total.counts is keyed by mark value only, so '0': 4 silently mixes section cleans and race wins.
misfits.suggestion: Allow counts to name what they count (counts_scope: sections | sections+race) or key counts by section kind.

misfits.what: 'Rider #' is a heat slot that changes between days and between qualifying and final (day 2 slots follow the day 1 result). entry.number and entry.start are entry-wide, so the slot is kept in x_rider_no_as_printed on each heat total.
misfits.suggestion: Add a per-part start record (total.start_slot or parts[].start_order[] of entry ids).

misfits.what: The qualifying ranking is not printed as a table: each heat block's Place column gives the rider's rank across all heats. The protocol needs a classification object, so one was assembled per day; it is printed data, but scattered.
misfits.suggestion: Allow a classification to declare 'assembled from part rows' (as_printed: 'Place column in heat blocks').

misfits.what: The Championship Results table prints only the top four although two more riders scored points. A classification has no way to say the printed list is truncated.
Championship results carry a Day 1 and Day 2 points column per row. row.points holds one value, so the per-day points went into x_day_points (they also sit on the day classifications).
misfits.suggestion: Allow row.components[] {part, value} for totals built from part results.

misfits.what: Day results mix sources: positions 1 to 4 from the Final, 5 to 8 from qualifying (day 1), and all from qualifying when the Final was cancelled (day 2). row.source_part expresses this well; noted as a fit, not a gap.
misfits.suggestion: Document source_part in the guide with this X-Trial example.

mapping.unread: Nothing unread. All three pages were read visually at 170 dpi; every heat total equals its six marks plus Race.
